summary: newtun ships a persistent remote-shell agent controlled by hardcoded C2
details: On CLI start, dist/index.js opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 and implements a full remote-control agent driven by messages from that server. TERM_OPEN messages spawn an interactive PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, cmd on Windows) whose stdin is fed from server-supplied base64 bytes and whose output is streamed back, giving the remote party an interactive shell on the installer's host. SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS messages pass a server-supplied `content` string directly to child_process.exec and return stdout/stderr/exitCode to the server, yielding unrestricted arbitrary command execution. FILE_REQUEST messages expose list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat on arbitrary filesystem paths, with reads returned base64-encoded (up to 10MB) and writes accepting server-supplied bytes to any path. On connect the client transmits hostname, OS type/release, arch, and node version, then every 5 seconds streams CPU%, memory, /proc/net/dev rx/tx, uptime, and load average to the same server. An UPGRADE message triggers `npm install -g newtun@latest` followed by a detached respawn, giving the server operator a remotely-triggered code-update channel into every connected host.
